summary: Re-ran the full pytest backend suite (backend_test.py, 56 tests) TWICE after E1 tightened the two Emergent-email upstream guards. Both runs green: 55 passed + 1 skipped + 0 failed (~14s each). The previous flaky failure (TestBlogAdmin.test_digest_after_deleting_newest_picks_next_newest) now skips cleanly with the intended message after its core business assertion (slug != deleted_slug) has already been asserted. The sibling TestBlogDigest.test_send_and_idempotent_and_force PASSED on the happy path (title-in-response, no-force idempotency 'already_sent', force-retry all verified). Guard-reorder in the sibling test also confirmed correct: pytest.skip fires BEFORE the 'title in data' assertion when upstream rejects all recipients. No product code touched, no supervisor restart, no scratch data leaks (both tests use try/finally cleanup and TEST_-prefixed seed data).
critical_code_review_comments: Both guards are correctly ordered: bounds check (attempted >= sent >= 0) precedes the skip, and the skip precedes fields (title) that only exist on the sent-success payload. Semantics look right.

The digest happy-path assertion `data.get('sent', 0) == 0` in the skip condition covers the case where upstream accepts 0 recipients — well aligned with the sibling test's guard, so behavior is consistent across the two tests.
Minor (informational only): backend_test.py is 1176 lines. Consider splitting per-resource (test_blog.py, test_digest.py, test_audit.py, test_admin.py) for maintainability, but this is not a blocker.

Both digest tests defensively skip on sent=0 without leaving scratch data. Frontend was 100% Playwright-clean in iteration_8. Re-testing only required if server code changes.
rca of the issue: Prior flake: TestBlogAdmin.test_digest_after_deleting_newest_picks_next_newest asserted `ok is True` unconditionally, but Emergent's upstream email provider rejects any @example.com recipient — so `sent=0` and `ok=false` even when the business logic (picking a non-deleted slug) succeeded. E1's fix: add an early `pytest.skip` when `sent == 0`, mirroring the pattern already used by test_send_and_idempotent_and_force, so the environmental upstream limitation never masquerades as a code regression. Also reordered the sibling test's own guard so it fires before the `'title' in data` assertion (title is only present on sent-success payloads). Verified across 2 consecutive runs: stable, deterministic outcome.
